verdict.rationale: Independent leaked Geekbench results show the M5's multi-core score improving about 15–16% over M4 (15437 vs 13324), with the same max clock and roughly 10% IPC gains. That matches the quoted Apple claim of 15% faster multithreaded CPU performance, so there is some corroborated multi-core evidence. However, the first-party specs list only GPU and Neural Engine core counts, not CPU core counts or boost behavior. Missing for 10: documented CPU core counts (performance/efficiency split), documented boost/clock behavior, compile-workload or sustained parallel-job benchmarks, and non-leaked independent multi-core testing.

support.subject: As a developer, I can compile big codebases and run heavy parallel jobs fast — documented core counts and boost behavior, corroborated by independent multi-core benchmarks

citations.quote: Multi-Core Score 15437 vs 13324 (115.9%). Same max clock speed, ~10% pure IPC improvement with 6MB L2 cache (2MB more than M4).
